```{r}
#| label: setup
if (!requireNamespace("rtists", quietly = TRUE)) {
  knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
} else {
  library(rtists)
  library(fiber)
}
```

## Overview

**rtists** (*R for Tissue Integrity Superimposed on Tractography Streamlines*)
provides interactive 3-D visualisation of tractography data defined in the
[fiber](https://github.com/tractoverse/fiber) package.  The central function is
`plot3d()`, a [S7](https://rconsortium.github.io/S7/) generic with methods for
the three core fiber classes:

| Class | Description |
|---|---|
| `fiber::streamline` | A single fibre tract — an ordered sequence of 3-D points plus optional metadata. |
| `fiber::bundle` | An ordered collection of streamlines representing a white-matter bundle. |
| `fiber::bundle_set` | A named collection of bundles, e.g. a whole tractogram or one tract per subject. |

The interactive figures are produced by the default three.js htmlwidget, so
they can be panned, rotated, and zoomed directly in the browser or the RStudio
/ Positron viewer pane.

---

## Data structures

A `streamline` stores three compartments, all accessible with the `@` operator:

- `@points` — an $n \times 3$ numeric matrix with columns `X`, `Y`, `Z`.
- `@point_data` — a named list of per-point numeric vectors (length $n$),
  e.g. fractional anisotropy (FA) sampled along the tract.
- `@streamline_data` — a named list of numeric scalars (length 1), e.g. a
  tract-level mean FA.

A `bundle` holds:

- `@streamlines` — a list of `streamline` objects.
- `@bundle_data` — a named list of bundle-level metadata.

### Creating a minimal example

```{r}
#| label: create-objects
pts <- matrix(
  c(
    0, 0, 0,
    1, 2, 1,
    2, 3, 3,
    3, 3, 5,
    4, 2, 6,
    5, 1, 7
  ),
  ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE,
  dimnames = list(NULL, c("X", "Y", "Z"))
)

sl <- streamline(
  points          = pts,
  point_data      = list(FA = c(0.25, 0.40, 0.65, 0.70, 0.55, 0.30)),
  streamline_data = list(mean_FA = 0.475)
)

sl
```

A bundle is just a list of streamlines wrapped by `bundle()`:

```{r}
#| label: create-bundle
# Simulate a small bundle of four slightly perturbed copies
set.seed(42)
streamlines <- lapply(seq_len(4), function(i) {
  noise <- matrix(rnorm(nrow(pts) * 3, sd = 0.15), ncol = 3)
  colnames(noise) <- c("X", "Y", "Z")
  streamline(
    points          = pts + noise,
    point_data      = list(FA = pmin(pmax(sl@point_data$FA + rnorm(6, sd = 0.05), 0), 1)),
    streamline_data = list(mean_FA = mean(sl@point_data$FA))
  )
})

bun <- bundle(streamlines)
bun
```

---

## Plotting with `plot3d()`

### Default: colour by local orientation

With no `color` argument, each point is coloured by the direction of the local
tangent vector.  Absolute values of the normalised $(dx, dy, dz)$ are mapped to
the R, G, B channels — the standard DTI convention (left–right = red,
anterior–posterior = green, superior–inferior = blue).

```{r}
#| label: fig-orientation
#| fig-cap: "Single streamline coloured by local fibre orientation."
plot3d(sl)
```

The same default works for a whole bundle:

```{r}
#| label: fig-bundle-orientation
#| fig-cap: "Bundle of four streamlines coloured by orientation."
plot3d(bun)
```

### Colour by per-point metadata

Pass any key from `@point_data` as the `color` argument.  Numeric values are
mapped to a continuous colour scale (default: `"Viridis"`).

```{r}
#| label: fig-point-fa
#| fig-cap: "Streamline coloured by per-point FA."
plot3d(sl, color = "FA")
```

### Colour by per-streamline metadata

Keys from `@streamline_data` are broadcast to every point of that streamline, 
so they work equally well as a colour aesthetic.  For a bundle this gives each
streamline a single uniform colour that reflects its tract-level scalar.

```{r}
#| label: fig-bundle-mean-fa
#| fig-cap: "Bundle coloured by per-streamline mean FA."
plot3d(bun, color = "mean_FA", palette = "RdYlBu")
```

### Fixed colour

Pass any CSS colour name or hex code to colour all lines identically.

```{r}
#| label: fig-fixed
#| fig-cap: "Bundle in a single fixed colour with reduced opacity."
plot3d(bun, color = "steelblue", opacity = 0.6)
```

---

## Appearance options

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `color` | `"orientation"` | Colour mode: `"orientation"`, metadata key, or a CSS/hex string. |
| `palette` | `"Viridis"` | Colour scale used for continuous numeric metadata (three.js resolves it via `hcl.colors()`). |
| `linewidth` | `NULL` | Line width. When `NULL` (default), the three.js backend auto-sizes the fast line path to ~0.5% of the scene's bounding-box diagonal, so lines read as hairlines at any spatial scale; an explicit numeric value is used as-is in world units. The plotly backend uses a fixed width of 2 px when left automatic. |
| `opacity` | `0.5` | Global line opacity (0–1). |
| `radius` | `NULL` | Tube radius. When `NULL` (default), rtists uses the radius carried in the object's own data if present (`radius` in the per-streamline or per-point data), or falls back to thin `Line2` lines when the streamlines carry none. A positive scalar draws every streamline as a true 3D tube at that fixed radius and overrides any data radius; per-streamline or per-point vectors give variable radii. rtists never shrinks tubes or hides streamlines to dodge overlap: overlapping tubes are the generator's business, not rtists's. |

Line width, opacity, and radius are combined freely:

```{r}
#| label: fig-layout
#| fig-cap: "Custom fixed colour, thicker lines, and reduced opacity."
plot3d(bun, color = "steelblue", linewidth = 4, opacity = 0.6)
```

---

## Static arclength projections with `plot2d()`

For a static publication figure, `plot2d()` re-parametrizes each streamline by
arc length — the distance travelled along the fibre — and draws the X, Y, and Z
coordinates against it in three vertically stacked ggplot2 facets. This makes
tract geometry directly comparable with per-point diffusion profiles: features
that line up at the same arclength actually occur at the same place on the
tract.

Geometries are downsampled into equal-arclength chunks (`n_chunks`, default
100) with one mean point per chunk, keeping figures light for long fibres. The
`color` argument accepts the same vocabulary as `plot3d()`: `"orientation"`
(DTI convention), a metadata key (continuous or categorical), or a fixed
CSS/hex colour.

```{r}
#| label: fig-plot2d
#| fig-cap: "Streamline arclength projection coloured by per-point FA."
plot2d(sl, color = "FA")
```

Pass a subset of `c("X", "Y", "Z")` as `facet` when only some coordinates are
of interest; additional arguments (e.g. `scales = "free_y"`) are forwarded to
`facet_wrap()`.

```{r}
#| label: fig-plot2d-bundle
#| fig-cap: "Bundle arclength projection, one line per streamline."
plot2d(bun, color = "mean_FA", palette = "RdYlBu")
```
